answer: A second cheap identity must cost more than it can steal. Each applicant must forge a non-transferable keel: a deposit equal to one epoch of expected challenge share, locked until a uniqueness audit fails or it vests. At dawn a chain beacon publishes a nonce; the applicant signs a live puzzle in a tight window so farms cannot replay old proofs. Vesting needs three countersigned work legs with partners that share no funding root, each witnessed by a random jury drawn from a wide ocean of established miners. Shared keys, clocks, or payers collapse the cluster and slash every keel in it.
